title: The Drift
question: Is what reviewers scrutinize a stable feature of peer review, or has it drifted over nine years?

figures.title: What reviewers inspect, 2018 → 2026
figures.deck: What reviewers inspect drifted over nine years, toward compute cost and statistical rigor.

claims.statement: The hygiene turn: compute cost (+3.2pp), statistical rigor (+3.0pp), baselines and reproducibility rise.
claims.derivation: object_share[object][2026] − object_share[object][2018], ×100, in percentage points; baselines_ablations and reproducibility also rise over the same span but are named without a printed pp figure in the caption

claims.statement: In relative terms, clarity's share fell 37%.

figures.title: The standards they invoke, 2018 → 2026
figures.deck: The standards they invoke drifted with it.

claims.statement: Among standards, the novelty standard and the presentation-as-trust standard — judging a paper's care by how it is written — each fall 3.5pp, while cost-benefit and claim-evidence matching climb.
claims.derivation: reasoning_share[standard][2026] − reasoning_share[standard][2018], ×100, in percentage points; cost_benefit and claim_evidence_match rise over the same span but are named without a printed pp figure in the caption

figures.title: The hardening: nine-year vitals
figures.deck: Three vital signs of the venue, read across nine years.

claims.statement: The share of post-response judgments that weaken or reverse has halved, 8.2% in 2018 (101 of 1,239 post-response units) to 4.2% in 2026 (1,799 of 43,267).
claims.derivation: (meta[year].weakened + meta[year].reversed) / meta[year].post_response_units, for 2018 and 2026. The deposition and the page previously printed 7.7% and 3.4%; no denominator in the shipped drift-data.json reproduces those, and the series was corrected to the shipped values 2026-08-26. The correction makes “halved” exact (a factor of 0.51) where the old pair overstated the fall.
claims.verified: claim recomputed from source island; series corrected, 2026-08-26

claims.statement: Negativity in the nine-year corpus holds near 77% all nine years (the 2026 corpus reads 71.8% — a different memo style, the same story).
claims.derivation: valence_share.negative[year], across all nine years, hovering in a narrow band around 0.77 (min 0.7485 in 2023, max 0.7907 in 2018)

figures.title: The currents: four distributions, nine years
figures.deck: Four distributions morphing through nine years — turn the dial, or stack the years like a mountain range.

claims.statement: The venue has used four scoring forms: ten labeled levels in 2018–19 and 2021, a four-point reject/weak-reject/weak-accept/accept form in 2020, a six-level ladder 2022–25, and even numbers only in 2026.
claims.derivation: distinct rating-scale shapes observed per year in the scores distribution, grouped into four eras

caveats.text: The share of units the labeller places in the same category on a held-out check is the same in the early years as in the late ones (0.81), so the drift measured here is a change in what reviewers wrote, not a change in how well the labels fit older text.
What the series cannot separate is reviewers changing from submissions changing: it measures what got written, not why.

The venue's scoring scale changed four times over 2018–2026 (ten labeled levels in 2018–19 and 2021, a four-point form in 2020, a six-level ladder 2022–25, even numbers only in 2026); because the rungs themselves moved, compare the shapes of the score distributions across years, not their raw positions.
caveats.scope: Fig. 26d SCORES GIVEN comparisons across years
